proposed.explanation:
You already hold 400 shares of ABUK (Abu Qir Fertilizers), which directly serves your stated goal of keeping a fertilizer exporter as a currency hedge. The verified earnings data supports continuing to hold: basic EPS for the nine months ended 30 Sep 2026 was 8.74 EGP, nearly double the 4.28 EGP for the same period a year earlier, indicating meaningful earnings growth. On a rough annualised basis (8.74 × 12/9 ≈ 11.65 EGP), the current price of 76.21 EGP implies a P/E of roughly 6.5×, which is not expensive for a commodity-linked exporter, though I caution that annualising nine-month results can be misleading if there is seasonality in fertiliser pricing.

I am not recommending a buy for two reasons. First, your ABUK position is already 30,484 EGP out of a 50,484 EGP total portfolio (≈ 60 %), so any additional purchase would breach the 50 % single-company concentration limit. Second, the evidence is limited to a single income-statement summary page; I have no balance-sheet data, no export-revenue breakdown (which is the key driver of the currency-hedge thesis), no dividend information, and no cash-flow statement to assess the durability of the earnings.

I am not recommending a sell because the verified figures show no deterioration: EPS more than doubled year-on-year, and there is no negative signal in the available evidence. With a five-year horizon, a separate emergency fund, and medium risk tolerance, holding a growing fertiliser exporter as a partial currency hedge is consistent with your profile.

Risks and uncertainties: fertiliser prices are cyclical and the strong 9M-2026 results may reflect a favourable price environment that could reverse. The most recent quarter's EPS (3M 2026) is flagged AMBIGUOUS in the source, so I cannot confirm whether the growth trend is still intact in the latest quarter. All absolute net-profit figures are also AMBIGUOUS due to a unit conflict on the page, so I could not independently verify the profit base. If you want a stronger currency-hedge position, you would need to diversify into other export-oriented names rather than add more ABUK, but that is outside the scope of the evidence provided. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.
